findings.finding: Figma has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by about 5.5-6% in each of the last two quarters. Q1 2026 came in at $333.4M against a $315-317M guide (+5.5%), Q2 at $370.1M against $348-350M (+6.0%), and Q4 2025 at $303.8M was above its range. The Q3 guide of $373-375M implies only about 1% sequential growth, against 11% from Q1 to Q2. On the call the CFO called it a 'snapshot' that excludes beta products, which he labelled upside. Repeating the pattern would give about $390-397M, 3-5% above the about $377M consensus, which sits only about 1% above the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, a 5.5% beat over the guide midpoint plus a $55M FY raise, closed +13.24% (2026-05-14). Q2 2026, a 6.0% beat plus a $40M FY raise, closed -14.85% (2026-08-05) on AI cost of revenue (+117%) and the soft Q3 sequential guide. A revenue beat by itself has not set the sign on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $376.6-379.7M sits only 0.7-1.5% above the guide midpoint, while the last two quarters beat by about 6%. If the sell-side had priced the pattern, consensus would be near $390M. The buy side probably expects a beat, which is why this is sized small and not at the implied move.
findings.independence: Q1 actual vs guide from a different document: Q4 2025 release (Q1 guide $315-317M, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579878/000162828026009024/fy25pressrelease.htm) and Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579878/000162828026035087/q126pressrelease.htm). CFO's 'beta excluded = upside' comment from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15392832623961088).

findings.finding: On 2026-08-25, partway through Q3, Figma gave 2x more AI credits on Professional and 1.6x on Organization/Enterprise add-ons at an unchanged price. The pay-as-you-go spending cap also stayed the same, so it now buys more usage. That is an effective per-credit price cut of about 50% and 37.5%. The CFO had said on 08-05 that most AI revenue comes through coterminous add-ons and warned a shift to pay-as-you-go would add variability. This lowers the AI-credit expansion and overage revenue per unit of usage for 5 weeks of Q3 and all of the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI monetization has moved the stock before: March 2026 credit-limit enforcement drew a selloff on churn/monetization fears (https://rallies.ai/news/figma-tumbles-as-march-ai-credit-enforcement-revives-churn-and-monetization-concerns). No earnings print has yet isolated AI-credit revenue as a line.
findings.why_not_priced: The change was posted on a help-centre page and a pricing tracker (https://usagepricing.com/blueprint/activity/figma-2026-08-25-packaging), not in a press release or an 8-K, and no analyst note I found quantifies it. If it were priced, previews would discuss lower AI add-on revenue in the Q4 guide; the Oct PT cuts cite gross margin, not this. Offsetting: it may lift usage and is probably partly in the Aug 5 guide if it was planned.
findings.independence: Same Figma help page as the agent-GA finding; the pricing tracker reads it as a price cut. Any revenue effect is my inference; the company has not quantified one.

findings.finding: The Figma agent in Design and Weave moved from open beta to general availability on 2026-10-06 and now consumes paid AI credits. The CFO said on 08-05 that beta and early-access products (agent, Make on local code, Motion and others) are excluded from guidance and would be upside once monetized. The Q4 guide given tonight is the first that can include a paid agent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises were bought in May (+13.24%) and sold in August (-14.85%). In August the sequential Q3 guide was the line cited as a deceleration worry.
findings.why_not_priced: The GA date appears on a support page, not in a press release, and no preview I found mentions it. If priced, Q4 consensus would sit above a run-rate extension of the Q3 guide. The guidance philosophy ('wait for sustained trends') means management may still keep it out of the Q4 guide, which caps this finding.
findings.independence: The CFO's statement that beta is excluded from guidance comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15392832623961088). The GA date shares a document with the credit-price-cut finding.

findings.finding: The guide already embeds deep H2 operating-margin compression. FY2026 non-GAAP operating income is guided at $125-135M and was maintained on 08-05. H1 delivered about $89M (Q1 about 16% of $333.4M, about $53M; Q2 $36.1M), so H2 is guided at about $41M on about $762M of revenue, roughly a 5% margin against about 13% in H1. A revenue beat at Figma's usual 85% gross margin clears that bar easily.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's -14.85% was attributed to profit reversal and AI cost (https://www.webull.com/news/15358948900545536). That is the line this name has traded on most recently, so a profit beat matters.
findings.why_not_priced: The implied H2 figure is arithmetic on the release and is not stated by the company. Q3 consensus EPS of about $0.05 non-GAAP (FXEmpire) is roughly consistent with the compressed guide, so a beat is not in the estimates. Preview commentary (Stifel's cut) focuses on GM falling from 90%+ to mid-80s, not on how low the operating-income bar sits.
findings.independence: Q1 non-GAAP margin of 16% from a separate summary of the Q1 release (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/figma-q1-2026-earnings-beat-110945684.html). Offset by the next finding (beta inference cost).

findings.finding: Q3 carried the full inference cost of the Figma agent and other beta features with no revenue, because the agent was free until GA on 10-06. The CFO said Figma 'bears the cost of inference' on beta and that gross margin 'will vary from quarter to quarter in the near term'. Q2 non-GAAP gross margin of 85% had risen 2.5 points q/q, so a Q3 step back is the risk on the line that sank the August print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: cost of revenue +117% and AI costs were cited for -14.85% (https://bingx.com/en/news/post/why-is-figma-fig-stock-price-down-today-august-rising-ai-costs-and-slower-growth-outlook-trigger-a-selloff).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Stifel's 10-14 cut cites gross margin falling to the mid-80s (https://www.itiger.com/news/1185028608), and the put skew pays for downside. Not priced is the specific point that the agent was unmonetized through the whole quarter while in open beta. Sized small because the operating-income bar above already absorbs much of it.
findings.independence: Help page dating the agent's GA to 10-06 (https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/42614902212887). Offsets the H2 margin-bar finding; both can be true.

findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not an informational edge. It is a squeeze mechanism that amplifies a positive surprise; at 3.85 days to cover it is modest, so the size is small.

findings.finding: Expansion signals softened in Q2. Net dollar retention fell to 136% from 139% in Q1. The CFO said customers are hiring below original plans because of AI productivity, while about two-thirds of $10K+ customers still added seats at renewal. He also flagged tougher Q3/Q4 comps from lapping the March 2025 pricing change. A further NDR decline is the seat-compression read the AI-disruption bears want.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NDR rose to 139% with the +13.24% May print and fell to 136% with the -14.85% August print; on this name it has gone with the reaction both times.
findings.why_not_priced: This is public since August, so the level is priced. The question is whether NDR keeps sliding. Peer read-through runs the other way: Atlassian reported no seat compression and broad seat expansion in August (https://parameter.io/atlassian-team-stock-rockets-30-following-record-breaking-quarterly-performance/). Hence small.
findings.independence: NDR 139% in Q1 from the Q1 release summary (https://marketchameleon.com/articles/b/2026/5/15/figma-accelerating-revenue-growth-ai-adoption-q1-2026).

findings.finding: Canva, Figma's largest design-platform competitor, cut its 2026 revenue-growth forecast from 30% to 20%. Q2 2026 revenue was $921.9M (+25.2%), and the CEO chose to slow AI rollouts to fix unit economics.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none: no Figma print has turned on a Canva data point.
findings.why_not_priced: Canva is private, so its numbers sit outside the sell-side models. The sign is ambiguous: it could mean less competitive AI pressure on Figma, or a category-wide AI cost squeeze. It is a proxy, so it is sized near zero.

baseline_tension: My net is mildly positive while the +11.76 put skew pays for downside and the 20-day run-up is flat. Why the options may be over-paying: the bar was trimmed (target cuts, Hold initiations), short interest of 12% is being covered, and the H2 operating-income guide is low. The August reaction shows that margin and guide quality can override a beat, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-pattern finding went from +1.5 to +1.0, because the same beat-and-raise was bought +13% in May and sold -15% in August.
Lesson 7 (skew): with a +11.8-point put skew against a net-positive set, p_up went from 53 to 52; the reason the options may be wrong is stated in baseline_tension.

Lessons 3, 5 and 6 left the rest standing. The two margin findings both hold and are kept apart. The Canva and Adobe proxies were already small. The bar is sourced to the company guide plus three agreeing estimates. Atlassian was already in outside_window.
